problemStatement.formal: Show that two equivalence relations can encode a three-place relative identity predicate satisfying the expected equivalence properties.
problemStatement.plain: Formalize Etter's claim that stereo equality, built from two equality relations, suffices for relative identity.
whyMatters: Gives a machine-checked bridge from philosophical relative identity to elementary equivalence-relation structure
Clarifies why one flat equivalence relation is too weak for viewpoint-dependent identity

proven: The stereoToRelative construction turns two equivalence relations into a valid relative identity predicate.
The relativeToStereo construction extracts a stereo pair from a relative identity predicate.
A single equivalence relation gives only flat identity, while two relations support nontrivial disagreement between viewpoints.
open: Study whether some relative identity structures require more than two equivalence relations.
